comments.author: cromwellian
comments.story: Quantum Entanglement Drives the Arrow of Time
comments.why: Clear, approachable explanation of spooky quantum phenomena via entanglement
comments.text: This Google Talk [VIDEO] uses entanglement and quantum information theory in a clear and understandable way to explain 'spooky' quantum phenomena, like the quantum eraser, de-coherence, the aspect experiment, and the measurement problem. Even if you don't know any QM, just basic algebra and calculus, it's really approachable. I used to be a fan of the Many Worlds interpretation, but after seeing this, I'm now a big fan of the Quantum Information Theory explanation. Starting about 43 minutes in, he goes into the QM Information Theory explanation, but I'd recommend watching the entire prezo. Link to my original post on the subject: [LINK]

comments.author: newpavlov
comments.story: Computer scientists prove that heat destroys quantum entanglement
comments.why: Good introduction to superdeterminism
comments.text: There is a very important and often forgotten caveat to the Bell's inequalities: it covers local hidden states. If we are to assume that measurement and particle creation apparatuses are entangled with each other (after all, they had plenty of opportunities since the big bang), then we have a global hidden state and the quantum measurment randomness becomes a simple artifact of removing global state from the picture. This interpretation of QM is usually called "superdeterminism" and, personally, I like it much more than the black vodoo measurement magic with collapsing wave functions or creation of whole new worlds on each tiny measurement. This video can be a good introduction to this topic: [VIDEO] (don't mind the clickbaity title, the video itself is good)

If you want to learn basics about it, I recommend watching this video: [VIDEO] Do not mind the (joking) clickbait title, the talk itself is quite good even if you only vaguely remember QM.

comments.author: replax
comments.story: A Schrödinger cat with eight lives: quantum entanglement of eight photons
comments.why: Ron Garret's talk arguing against the Copenhagen interpretation
comments.text: In fact, the Copenhagen interpretation has been proven wrong by fellow lisper Ron Garret. You can read his paper here: www.flownet.com/ron/QM.pdf and watch his google talk about it [VIDEO] . The problem is, that most people (not scientists, mind you) do not really care anyway, and the Copenhagen interpretation gives you a nice story to tell, which is fairly "strange", yet somewhat understandable. I hate the fact that even science magazines still 100% subscribe to the Copenhagen interpretation, just to attract a greater readership and to be able to use catchier headlines.

comments.author: themgt
comments.story: Interpretations of quantum theory: A map of madness
comments.why: Source for Garret's zero-worlds interpretation
comments.text: Mermin put it perhaps most succinctly, that reality is "correlations without correlata", or as Ron Garret coined, the "zero-worlds interpretation"[1] It also makes sense to me on a sociological level, that the way in which this interpretation seems to undermine the very foundation of western, scientific thought is the reason it has been so desperately avoided for so long, with many preferring to believe in an infinite forking (but somehow still "real) multiverse, than the idea that reality itself is intersubjective.
